text: According to the chapter's discussion of data leakage, what is the most common and serious methodological pitfall in evaluating biological machine learning models?
choices: Using a naive random train/test split so that homologous sequences end up in both sets, inflating measured performance
Applying SHAP values to explain a tree-based model
Using stratified k-fold cross-validation to preserve class balance
explanation: Data leakage most commonly arises when a naive random split places homologous sequences in both training and test sets, artificially inflating performance; the recommended fix is splitting by protein family, species, or sequence cluster. Using many CV folds and stratified k-fold CV are legitimate, recommended practices rather than pitfalls, and SHAP is a valid interpretability tool, not a source of leakage.
